title: Almost-sure support on two points
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and let $x,y\in\mathbb R$ be distinct. If $\mu(X=x)+\mu(X=y)=1$, then $X$ belongs to $\{x,y\}$ almost surely.
replaced: Let $X$ be a measurable real random variable on a probability space and let $x\ne y$. If $\Pr[X=x]+\Pr[X=y]=1$, then $X\in\{x,y\}$ almost surely.
